messages.author: 9a06c60161510efe
messages.subject: High autocorrelation on parameters
parts: Hi, I am trying to run the attached model. Unfortunately, I find that the parameters of interest "upsilon_intercept" and "beta_quiz" are highly autocorrelated. Is there any way to re-write the model that would make this problem less severe?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] High autocorrelation on parameters
parts:
It's not unusual for the intercept and slope of a regression to
be correlated. Centering the variable quiz should help; if the
values are all positive or negative, the problem's much worse.

I would also recommend adding weakly informative priors; it can
help quite a bit when parameters are only weakly identified.

- Bob


P.S.

What you're calling "upsilon_normal" should be called
"logit_upsilon", because it's the log odds of upsilon.
And speaking of logit,

1 / (1 + exp(-upsilon_normal[i]))

should be

inv_logit(upsilon_normal[i])

All those ~ statements to increment the log density
should be vectorized. It'll be *a lot* faster.

Also, given that Y_mid and Y_min are data, you don't need an
explicit truncation (it only contributes a constant to the log
density). The constraint on alpha makes sure you're in support.
